app.title: ExonViz (web form)
app.summary: A person types a gene name, a transcript identifier or an HGVS variant description into a form, sets how the figure should be drawn (exon height, scale per base pair, gaps, wrapping width, which exons, colours, whether to show non-coding parts and exon numbers, pin or bar variant marks) and submits. The page draws every exon of the transcript to scale, wrapped into rows, with exon ends notched or pointed by reading-frame phase and each variant marked at its position with a colour legend. Variants that fall outside the drawn exons are reported by name, and a download link saves the figure as an SVG file named after the transcript.

task.text: Draw a to-scale figure of a transcript's exons, their reading frames and where given variants fall, and save it as an SVG.

data.text: One transcript's exon structure and coding region, fetched for a typed identifier, plus zero or more variants written in standard nomenclature, each placed at a position along the exons.
data.item: an exon of a transcript, with its size, coding part, reading-frame phases at each end and any variants inside it

stage.text: drawing figures of already-described variants on a transcript, for papers and case reports

mechanism.text: A sidebar form holds the identifier and every drawing option; submitting it redraws the SVG figure beside it as a wrapped sequence track of exons with variant marks and a legend, and builds a download link that re-renders the same figure from the same settings as a file. Messages above the page report variants that could not be placed and drawing errors.

field.text: transcript and variant diagrams in human molecular genetics

workflow.name: draw a to-scale diagram of a sequence with marked positions and save it as a figure

steps.here: Type a gene name, a versioned transcript or an HGVS description (one variant or several in brackets); a table of example inputs sits above the form. Gene names are swapped for their MANE Select transcript, a bare transcript becomes a variant-free description, and multiple variants are sorted by position.

steps.step: filter to the items that matter
steps.here: First-exon and last-exon fields cut the transcript to a range of exons, and the 'Show non-coding' checkbox keeps or trims the untranslated parts.

steps.step: set how the figure is drawn
steps.here: Exon height, pixels per base pair, gap between exons, maximum figure width, exon colour, a space-separated list of variant colours to cycle through, exon numbers on or off, and pin or bar variant marks.

steps.step: compute a value from the data
steps.here: On submit the exon and coding coordinates are looked up, each variant is mapped to a position inside an exon, and each exon's start and end reading-frame phase is carried over from the one before it.

steps.step: look over every item at a glance
steps.here: All chosen exons are drawn to scale in rows that wrap at the figure width, with phase-shaped ends, coloured variant pins or bars and a legend of variant names.

steps.step: see what could not be included
steps.here: A banner lists the variants dropped because they fall outside the drawn exons, or the error that stopped the drawing, such as a scale too small for the phase caps.
'Download!' re-renders the figure from the submitted settings and saves it as an SVG named after the transcript.

distinctive: Each exon's ends are drawn flat, notched or pointed by its reading-frame phase, so whether neighbouring exons keep the frame can be read off the figure.
Input follows HGVS nomenclature, and a bundled gene-to-MANE-Select table lets a bare gene name stand in for its reference transcript.
Variants that land in introns, outside the chosen exon range or in hidden non-coding parts are dropped and named back to the person.
Exons are split across rows only at points that keep the phase caps whole, and a minimum scale is enforced so the caps fit.
